name: Market Snapshot CLI
blurb: A typed, validated, logged Typer CLI that reads an instruments fixture, filters it, computes summary stats and writes a report without dying on corrupt rows.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: src/aie_lab layout visible from the repo root, uv.lock committed, and a v0.1.0 tag on the commit that first runs end to end.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Open with the problem: raw instrument feeds are messy and you need one trustworthy summary command, then show install and the exact snapshot invocation.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Paste the terminal output of a normal run and of the corrupt-fixture run so the quarantine behaviour is visible, not just claimed.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: Tests cover parsing, exchange and currency filtering and the quarantine path, and the README says how to run them in one line.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: One paragraph on why Pydantic guards the boundary while dataclasses carry internal state, and why config comes from .env.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: Say plainly that it reads a local fixture rather than a live feed, and that the cache has a fixed TTL with no invalidation hook.

checklist.label: Future improvements listed
checklist.hint: Name the next two concrete steps, such as swapping the fixture for a real filings endpoint and adding a --format md report.

name: Concurrent Filings Fetcher
blurb: An async fetcher that pulls many tickers under bounded concurrency with tenacity retries, validates every response and proves the speed-up with numbers.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: Work landed through a branch and a self-reviewed pull request, so the history shows the professional flow you learned this week.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: State the problem as twenty sequential network calls costing twenty seconds, then show the gather-with-semaphore answer.

checklist.label: Architecture diagram
checklist.hint: An ASCII sketch is fine: client to semaphore to retry wrapper to validator to quarantine and report file.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: respx covers 200, 404, 500 and timeout paths offline, plus one flaky-simulation test proving 500-500-200 succeeds.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Explain the concurrency cap of five, and why retries fire on 5xx and timeouts but never on a 404.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish the real wall-clock table: twenty tickers concurrent versus sequential, measured on your machine, with the ratio.

checklist.label: Future improvements listed
checklist.hint: Name what you would do next, such as swapping the stand-in public API for a real filings provider behind the same client interface.

name: Notes API, Deployed
blurb: A CRUD notes service with API-key auth, per-key rate limits, idempotent create, request ids and an error envelope, running on a public URL.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: Routers, services and models are split into packages so a reviewer can find the auth dependency in under a minute.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Frame it as the smallest honest production API: authenticated, rate limited and safe to retry, then link the live URL and /docs.

checklist.label: Live deployment URL
checklist.hint: The Render URL answers the health check path, and the README is honest that free-tier cold starts add several seconds to the first call.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Include the curl demo script output: create with an idempotency key, replay it, and show the identical response body.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: TestClient suite proves 401 without a key, the 422 envelope shape, and a 429 with Retry-After after a burst.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Explain the idempotency key store and its TTL, and why the error envelope carries a request id instead of a stack trace.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: Say that persistence is a JSON file, that the rate limiter is per process, and name what breaks when a second instance starts.

name: Structured Extractor API
blurb: A POST /extract service turning messy text into schema-validated JSON through the resilient LLM client, with a repair path and per-request cost logging.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: The schema registry (deal, contact, invoice) sits in its own module so adding a fourth schema is obviously a small change.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Lead with the business problem: free text into typed records that downstream systems can insert without a human reading them.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Show one request and response pair including a field left null because the source text genuinely lacked it.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: Every test runs offline against fixture model responses, including one malformed reply that proves the repair path recovers.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Explain why the Pydantic schema is the prompt contract, and why optional fields beat forcing the model to invent values.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish the measured cost per thousand requests from your ledger, with the token counts and model that produced it.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: State the extraction accuracy you have actually observed on your own samples, and that there is no gold set behind it yet.

name: TriageDesk Support Triage
blurb: A support-email service that classifies, extracts entities, looks up the customer through a tool call and streams a drafted reply with a confidence field.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: Prompts live in a prompts/ directory with version notes, not buried in f-strings inside the handlers.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Open with the cost of manual triage: a queue of raw emails, and the minutes per ticket your service removes.

checklist.label: Architecture diagram
checklist.hint: A mermaid diagram of ingest, classify, extract, customer_lookup tool call, draft and stream, with the validation step marked.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Record the streaming draft endpoint with curl -N so the reader sees tokens arriving, not a still frame of finished text.

checklist.label: Live deployment URL
checklist.hint: Deploy with a demo API key and a sample ticket in the README so a reviewer can trigger a real triage in one command.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: The LLM is mocked throughout, and edge cases are pinned: empty email, a ten-thousand-word rant, and an instruction-injection attempt.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Justify the model tier per stage, the confidence field's meaning, and why the tool result contract returns not_found rather than guessing.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: Admit that the customer database is a fixture, and that the injection attempt is flagged rather than fully neutralised at this stage.

checklist.label: Future improvements listed
checklist.hint: Name the queue for slow drafts and a gold set of labelled tickets as the next two moves, in that order.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish cost per ticket from the ledger and the p95 latency of the classify-and-extract path across your sample emails.

name: Ask-My-Docs v1
blurb: A CLI and endpoint answering questions over your own PDF corpus with citations, metadata filters, honest refusals and a committed 25-case gold set.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: gold.jsonl is committed at the repo root level where a reviewer trips over it, because the gold set is the interesting artifact.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Name the documents you indexed and the questions people actually ask of them, then show ingest and ask commands.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Show one answered question with its citations and one unanswerable question where the system refuses cleanly.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: Tests prove chunk ids in citations resolve to real chunks, and that the five unanswerable gold cases return a refusal.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish the gold set shape: 25 cases split across easy, medium, hard and unanswerable, with your first eyeballed hit rate.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Explain your chunk size and overlap choice against the broken-sentence rate you measured, and why metadata filtering exists.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: State that retrieval is dense-only for now, and that vocabulary mismatch between question and document is a known miss.

name: DocQA Productionized
blurb: The evaluated DocQA service: upload and ingest, hybrid retrieval with reranking, cited answers with confidence, auth, rate limits and a one-command eval suite.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: run_evals.py sits beside the app code and runs from a single command documented in the README.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Lead with the question your corpus answers for a real reader, then the metrics table, then how to run it.

checklist.label: Architecture diagram
checklist.hint: Diagram the two paths separately: ingest (upload, chunk, embed, index) and ask (rewrite, hybrid, rerank, pack, answer).

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Screenshot an answer with citations next to the eval summary output, so quality and measurement appear together.

checklist.label: Live deployment URL
checklist.hint: A public instance with a seeded read-only corpus, and a note that ingest is disabled on the demo tenant.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: Unit tests plus eval thresholds as assertions, so a bad retrieval change fails the suite rather than shipping quietly.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish the money table: baseline, hybrid, hybrid plus rerank with recall@5, MRR, groundedness and added latency per stage.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Justify retrieving twenty and reranking to five, and the judge rubric you calibrated against your own hand labels.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: Report the judge agreement percentage honestly and name the failure categories still present in your worst five cases.

checklist.label: Future improvements listed
checklist.hint: Point at the queue and Postgres upgrade coming in week nine, and any gold cases you know are still too easy.

name: Research Agent
blurb: A from-scratch agent over your document corpus with tools, a scratchpad, an approval gate on saving reports, a trace viewer and a ten-task eval.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: The loop is one readable file of roughly fifty lines, because being able to point at it is the whole claim.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: State the multi-part questions the agent handles, and include the workflow-versus-agent verdict paragraph with its numbers.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Paste a pretty-printed transcript showing tool calls, the scratchpad note and the approval gate pausing on save_report.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: Tests cover the max-steps guard, the repeated-call detector, and both the approve and deny paths of the gate.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish the eval result as at least seven of ten tasks passing, with mean cost and mean steps per task.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Explain the sandbox corpus directory, the tool allowlist and the cost cap, and why the loop has no framework under it.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: Write up one failure with its root cause from your taxonomy, such as a premature stop or an ignored piece of evidence.

name: DocQA Platform Upgrade
blurb: DocQA grown into a platform: async ingestion through arq workers, Postgres persistence, Redis cache and limits, webhook intake and a live stats endpoint.

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: Migrations are in version control and the seed script runs against a clean database without manual SQL.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Explain what broke at the previous design: a request handler doing minutes of embedding work behind a sixty-second timeout.

checklist.label: Architecture diagram
checklist.hint: Show API, queue, worker, Postgres, Redis and vector store with the job id flowing from POST /documents to GET /jobs/{id}.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: Capture the upload returning a job id instantly, then the status endpoint moving through progress to done.

checklist.label: Live deployment URL
checklist.hint: Deploy at least the API publicly, and document which components run where and what the demo tenant is allowed to do.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: Include the invariant test: enqueue the same document twice and prove exactly one processing run through the SETNX guard.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish the stats endpoint numbers: cache hit rate, average latency, documents and queries processed, and cost per query.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Explain the cache key including the index version, and why webhook handlers verify, dedupe and enqueue rather than process.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: Name the dual-write gap you have not closed and the absence of a dead-letter queue for jobs that exhaust retries.

checklist.label: Future improvements listed
checklist.hint: Point to containerisation, tracing and tenant isolation as the next week's work, with the one you consider most urgent first.

name: Athena Enterprise Knowledge Assistant

checklist.label: GitHub repo public
checklist.hint: ADR-001 is committed in the repo alongside the milestone history, so the reasoning is as readable as the result.

checklist.label: README with problem statement
checklist.hint: Write for a hiring manager with ninety seconds: the firm's problem, the demo link, then the metrics table above the fold.

checklist.label: Architecture diagram
checklist.hint: One mermaid diagram covering tenant-scoped ingestion, retrieval, assistant tools and the observability path, matching the deployed code.

checklist.label: Screenshots or demo GIF
checklist.hint: A three-minute walkthrough following the demo script: the ask, the cited answer, the eval table, then the architecture.

checklist.label: Live deployment URL
checklist.hint: A public instance with a seeded safe demo tenant, deploy-on-main proven by one trivial change reaching the URL.

checklist.label: Tests passing
checklist.hint: The suite includes the permanent tenant-isolation test proving user A cannot retrieve user B's document, plus the injection mitigations.

checklist.label: Metrics/eval numbers published
checklist.hint: Publish recall@5, groundedness, p95 latency and cost per query from the full eval run, with the date and model they were measured on.

checklist.label: Design decisions documented
checklist.hint: Summarise the ADR in the README: why this retrieval stack, why arq over alternatives, and what you deliberately did not build.

checklist.label: Known limitations documented
checklist.hint: State residual injection risk honestly, the corpus scale you actually tested, and where cold starts or rate limits bite.

checklist.label: Future improvements listed
